headline: Blue Planet III keeps rough footage to prove it isn't AI-made
summary: BBC's Blue Planet III deliberately includes cloudier, less polished, "more organic" shots to assure viewers its animals are real rather than AI-generated, a shift from earlier series known for crystal-clear footage, since overly polished imagery is now seen as a possible sign of AI.

claims.statement: BBC's Blue Planet III deliberately keeps less-polished, "more organic" footage to show it isn't AI-generated.

sources.quote: BBC series deliberately uses ‘more organic’ shots to assure viewers animals are not AI-generated, producers say
Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI

claims.statement: Earlier Blue Planet series were known for very polished, crystal-clear footage.

sources.quote: Previous incarnations of the nature series were defined by their gorgeous, crystal-clear footage that seemed almost too good to be real.

claims.statement: Overly polished, seamless footage is now seen as a potential giveaway of AI generation.

sources.quote: one dead giveaway of AI is when things look too polished and seamless
